summary.headline: 9 finding(s); most severe: No price found in the raw HTML of 2 page(s) that should carry one

findings.title: No price found in the raw HTML of 2 page(s) that should carry one
findings.evidence: 2 page(s) whose URL/role commits them to state a price contain no price-shaped token anywhere in the raw response - not in visible text, JSON-LD, meta tags, or any hydration payload. Examples: ['https://www.rhs.org.uk/shop/garden-centres (role=product)', 'https://www.rhs.org.uk/shop/licensed-products (role=product)']. Reproduce: curl -s 'https://www.rhs.org.uk/shop/garden-centres' | grep -Eo '[$£€¥₹][ ]?[0-9]|[0-9][ ]?(€|EUR|USD|GBP|CHF|kr)'

suggested_action.summary: Render the price into server-side HTML text on these pages.
how: Emit the price as plain text in the server response, not only after client-side JavaScript runs.
If the value is loaded from an API at runtime, server-render a default and hydrate over it, so the HTML is never empty of the fact.
Additionally express it in structured data (Product/Offer for price, LocalBusiness/ContactPoint for phone).
suggested_action.verify: curl -s <url> | grep -i '<price value>' returns a match with JavaScript disabled.

detail.measured_on: raw HTTP response, no JavaScript executed
detail.limit: If this value is fetched by client-side XHR after load, a human in a browser sees it and a non-rendering retrieval agent does not. The finding stands for the agent; verify with JavaScript disabled, not by viewing the page in a browser.

findings.title: Brand identity is not anchored to any external profile
findings.evidence: None of the 12 crawled page(s) declares Organization, LocalBusiness or similar structured data with sameAs links. Without sameAs, an assistant has nothing distinguishing this brand from others sharing the name, which is the standard cause of mistaken identity.

suggested_action.summary: Publish Organization JSON-LD with sameAs links to authoritative profiles.
how: Add Organization markup with "sameAs": [Wikidata, LinkedIn, Crunchbase, and your primary social profiles].
Use the identical legal/brand name across title tags, markup and body copy.
suggested_action.verify: Rich Results Test shows Organization with a populated sameAs array.

findings.title: Interactive controls without an accessible name on 12 page(s)
findings.evidence: https://www.rhs.org.uk/: 6/221 controls expose no text, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, SVG title or image alt; https://www.rhs.org.uk/about-us/contact-us: 6/389 controls expose no text, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, SVG title or image alt; https://www.rhs.org.uk/about-us: 6/199 controls expose no text, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, SVG title or image alt; https://www.rhs.org.uk/shop/garden-centres: 9/200 controls expose no text, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, SVG title or image alt. Controls whose name is bound by a JS framework (v-, x-, ng-, :, @, [) were assumed named at runtime and not counted.

suggested_action.summary: Give every control a name a machine can read.
how: Add visible text, or aria-label where the control is icon-only.
An unnamed control is unusable with a screen reader and invisible to any agent trying to understand what actions the page offers.
suggested_action.verify: Every button/link resolves to a non-empty accessible name.

findings.title: Images missing alt attributes on 4 page(s)
findings.evidence: https://www.rhs.org.uk/about-us: 5/11 images have no alt attribute; https://www.rhs.org.uk/about-us/commercial-opportunities: 5/11 images have no alt attribute; https://www.rhs.org.uk/about-us/our-people: 6/12 images have no alt attribute; https://www.rhs.org.uk/about-us/support-us/leave-a-gift-in-your-will: 4/9 images have no alt attribute. Tracking pixels, images inside <noscript> and images marked presentational or aria-hidden are not counted.

suggested_action.summary: Add alt text to content images; use alt="" for decorative ones.
how: Describe what the image conveys, not that it is an image.
If a price, specification table or contact detail exists only inside an image, restate it as text: retrieval agents do not read images.
Decorative images should carry an explicit empty alt="" so assistive tech skips them.
suggested_action.verify: No content lacks an alt attribute entirely.

findings.title: Key facts exist only inside script payloads on 1 page(s)
findings.evidence: https://www.rhs.org.uk/about-us/contact-us: phone '28.685969' found only in application/json, absent from extracted text

suggested_action.summary: Promote these facts from the hydration payload into server-rendered text.
how: The value is in the bytes, so a determined parser could reach it - but boilerplate extractors strip <script> before the model sees the page, so in practice it is invisible.
Server-render the same value into visible prose, and also state it in JSON-LD, which the indexing crawlers that build the search index assistants query do read.
suggested_action.verify: The value appears in the output of a text-extraction tool (e.g. `python -c "import trafilatura,sys;print(trafilatura.extract(sys.stdin.read()))"`).

findings.title: No Product structured data on 2 product page(s)
findings.evidence: 2/12 crawled product pages carry no Product JSON-LD, so the price, availability and identity of the item are stated only in prose, if at all. Examples: ['https://www.rhs.org.uk/shop/garden-centres', 'https://www.rhs.org.uk/shop/licensed-products']. Structured data is read by the indexing crawlers that build the search index assistants query.

suggested_action.summary: Add Product JSON-LD with an Offer to each product page.
how: Product -> name, description, sku, image, offers{price, priceCurrency, availability}.
Render the same price in the visible text, from the same source of truth.
suggested_action.verify: A schema.org validator reports a Product with an Offer and no errors.

findings.title: No usable XML sitemap discovered
findings.evidence: robots.txt declared 10 sitemap(s) and /sitemap.xml yielded no parsable <loc> entries. Crawlers then rely entirely on link discovery.

suggested_action.summary: Publish an XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt.
how: Generate /sitemap.xml listing every canonical URL with an accurate <lastmod>.
Add 'Sitemap: https://<host>/sitemap.xml' to robots.txt.

findings.title: No canonical link on 2 duplicate-prone page(s)
findings.evidence: 2/12 product, pricing or blog pages declare no <link rel="canonical">. Examples: ['https://www.rhs.org.uk/shop/garden-centres', 'https://www.rhs.org.uk/shop/licensed-products']. Without one, tracking parameters and trailing-slash variants of the same page compete as separate URLs.

suggested_action.summary: Give every indexable page a self-referencing canonical URL.
how: Add <link rel="canonical" href="<absolute self URL>"> to each page.
suggested_action.verify: Each page's canonical resolves to itself with HTTP 200.

detail.note: A missing canonical is a hygiene gap, not a blocker: an indexer picks a URL on its own, usually the one it crawled.

findings.title: No structured data on 2 significant page(s)
findings.evidence: 2/12 crawled pages of type ['about', 'home'] contain no JSON-LD. Structured data is read by the indexing crawlers that build the search index assistants query, and it states a fact with a type attached. Examples: ['https://www.rhs.org.uk/', 'https://www.rhs.org.uk/about-us']

suggested_action.summary: Add schema.org JSON-LD appropriate to each page type.
how: Homepage/About -> Organization with name, url, logo, description, sameAs.
Pricing -> Product or Service per tier, or an Offer list.
Article/blog -> Article with headline, datePublished, dateModified, author.
suggested_action.verify: A schema.org validator reports a detected item type with no errors.

ai_policy.interpretation: Blocking training agents is a licensing choice and does not affect whether assistants can cite you. Only retrieval agents gate citation.

checks_skipped.reason: Not assessed: whether independent third parties agree with this site's claims. Reason: that needs a search backend, which this marketplace does not assume. How to check it yourself: search your brand plus a key fact (price, founding year, HQ) and count independent sources that agree.
checks_skipped.impact: Claims that exist only on this site are not distinguished from claims corroborated across the web. The on-site corroboration checks still ran.

checks_skipped.reason: Not assessed: anything behind a login, checkout step or account area. Reason: the audit is read-only and never authenticates, submits a form or creates an account.
checks_skipped.impact: How to check it yourself: walk the signup, checkout or booking flow on a phone with a test account and count the required steps and fields.

checks_skipped.reason: Not assessed: behaviour metrics (bounce rate, dwell time, scroll depth, conversion rate). Reason: they are observed, not inferred from markup, and a short visit from an AI answer is often a success - the visitor came to verify one fact and did.
checks_skipped.impact: How to check it yourself: in your analytics, segment sessions by referrer (chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, claude.ai) and compare their conversion rate, not their bounce rate, with search traffic.

checks_skipped.reason: Not assessed: colour contrast (WCAG 1.4.3). Reason: contrast ratios need computed styles, which need a browser; this marketplace runs without one to stay portable and deterministic.
checks_skipped.impact: How to check it yourself: run axe DevTools or Lighthouse on the top 3 page templates and read the contrast section.

checks_skipped.reason: Not assessed: copy quality, persuasion and jargon. Reason: subjective; no static threshold separates plain language from marketing copy across industries and languages without a high false-positive rate.
checks_skipped.impact: How to check it yourself: read the first paragraph of the homepage and one product page aloud to someone outside the company and ask what the site offers and for whom.

checks_skipped.reason: Not assessed: Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP). Reason: these are field metrics at the 75th percentile; a single synthetic fetch is not a measurement and INP cannot be measured synthetically at all.
checks_skipped.impact: How to check it yourself: open Google Search Console's Core Web Vitals report, which uses real-user data, or run Lighthouse for lab LCP/CLS.

checks_skipped.reason: Not assessed: the rendered experience (overlay and cookie-banner timing, tap target size, focus visibility, layout at phone width). Reason: all of it depends on CSS and JavaScript executing, which needs a browser.
checks_skipped.impact: How to check it yourself: run Lighthouse and axe on the top 3 templates at phone width, then tab through each page once to confirm focus is visible.

proactive_recommendations.title: Publish an llms.txt describing your site for AI clients
proactive_recommendations.rationale: An emerging convention: a short, stable, plain-text map of what your site covers and where the authoritative pages are. Cheap to add, and it gives retrieval agents an unambiguous starting point.
proactive_recommendations.applies_because: GET /llms.txt did not return a plain-text document

proactive_recommendations.title: Decide your AI-crawler policy deliberately, and write it down
proactive_recommendations.rationale: Training access and retrieval access are separate decisions. Blocking training crawlers while explicitly allowing retrieval agents is a coherent, defensible position - but it has to be configured on purpose, per user-agent.
proactive_recommendations.applies_because: robots.txt names no AI retrieval or training agent, so the current policy is whatever the wildcard group happens to say

proactive_recommendations.title: Add a machine-readable FAQ layer shaped for quotation
proactive_recommendations.rationale: FAQPage structured data pairs a question with a self-contained answer. That is exactly the shape an assistant wants to lift, and it survives text extraction.
proactive_recommendations.applies_because: no crawled page carries FAQPage JSON-LD

proactive_recommendations.title: Publish a stable, citable facts page
proactive_recommendations.rationale: Founding date, leadership, HQ, product line, pricing - in one durable URL that third parties can cite verbatim. Corroboration across independent sources is what makes a claim credible to a machine, and you can seed it.
proactive_recommendations.applies_because: no crawled page declares Organization sameAs links, so there is no anchor for third parties to corroborate against

already_in_place.title: Server-render your most-quoted facts even inside a SPA
already_in_place.because: not a client-rendered app, or a specific finding already covers it

already_in_place.title: Answer the question visitors arrive with on the first screen
already_in_place.because: the homepage's first 60 words already name the site or state a concrete figure

already_in_place.title: Every deep page links to its parent section and a contact route
already_in_place.because: every substantial deep page already links onward from its content

limits: Not assessed: behaviour metrics (bounce rate, dwell time, scroll depth, conversion). Reason: a crawl sees markup, never visitors; engagement findings are structural risk factors, capped at medium for that reason. How to check it yourself: in your analytics, segment sessions by referrer (chatgpt.com, perplexity.ai, claude.ai) and compare their conversion rate with search traffic.

Not assessed: the rendered experience (layout, overlays and cookie banners, colour contrast, Core Web Vitals) and facts loaded by client-side requests after page load. Reason: no JavaScript is executed and no browser is used - which is also what non-rendering AI retrieval agents see; a fact fetched only by XHR can be a false negative here. How to check it yourself: run Lighthouse and axe on the top three templates, and open a key page with JavaScript disabled to see what a bot gets.

Not assessed: copy quality - whether the words persuade, or answer the visitor's question well. Reason: subjective, with no static threshold that holds across industries and languages; the scripted checks measure only structure and vocabulary overlap. How to check it yourself: read the first paragraph of the homepage and one product page to someone outside the company and ask what the site offers and for whom.

Not assessed: anything behind a login, checkout step or account area. Reason: the audit is read-only and never authenticates, submits a form or creates an account. How to check it yourself: walk the signup, checkout or booking flow with a test account and count the required steps and fields.

Not assessed: personalization of AI answers (appendix E). Reason: it happens inside the assistant, from the user's own context, and no site-side measurement exists; the site-side lever - self-contained, quotable facts - is what the extraction and quotability checks cover. How to check it yourself: ask an assistant the same question about your brand in a fresh session and in a long-running one, and compare.

Not assessed: cross-web corroboration - whether independent sources agree with the site's facts. Reason: it needs a search backend and off-site fetches, which this audit does not make; only on-site corroboration hooks (sameAs, press links) are checked. How to check it yourself: search Wikipedia, Wikidata, Crunchbase and the press for your founding date, HQ, leadership and pricing, and reconcile differences.

Not assessed: problems outside the scripted checks, unless an agent review ran (see agent_review). Reason: a fixed list of checks misses what it does not list. How to check it yourself: follow agent-review-audit/SKILL.md; every claim it admits was checked against the crawl and is capped at low severity.
